findings.title: Part B treats any successful tool call as "read the rest", but the plan says "read files"
findings.description:
The plan entry (900-slices:442) keeps a truncated diff as a normal verdict only when "the model did read files". D4 checks for something weaker: `(tool_calls_made or 0) - (failed_tool_calls or 0) > 0`, so any successful call counts. That includes one `Glob`/`list_files` or a `Grep` that never opens the omitted files. A model that makes one directory listing and then returns PASS on a truncated diff skips the cap and gives a clean PASS. That is close to the #135 failure this slice exists to prevent.

The design should do one of two things:
- Limit the count to file-reading tools. This works only if tool telemetry records tool names, and the design should say whether it does.
- State openly that any call counts, because the count telemetry can't tell tools apart, and record that this accepts the gap the plan describes. Walkthrough step 3 would then need to check which tool was called, not only that `toolCallsMade > 0`.

The plan's success criterion SC5 ("at least one successful tool call → verdict unchanged") has the same weakness.

findings.title: No stated handling when the final stamped message never arrives
findings.description:
`answering_models` is stamped only on the final Message: the SDK `ResultMessage` translation, and OpenAI's `_stamp_tool_telemetry`. If the stream hangs, times out or disconnects after assistant messages have arrived but before that final message, the models already seen are thrown away. D11 then writes "Answering model: not reported by provider (aiModel is the requested id)". That sentence is false here, because the provider did report a model and squadron dropped it. That is exactly the "artifact states the request, not the run" problem this slice is meant to fix.

The design mentions `ended_mid_task` and the #92 recovery turn, but it never covers a partial first turn. It should state which artifact (if any) a cut-off stream produces. If it does produce a `ReviewResult` artifact, there are two options:
- Stamp the models as they are seen, not only at the end.
- Have the digest wording tell "provider reported nothing" (Codex) apart from "turn ended before the stamp".

Either way, add a stubbed-stream test that cuts the stream after one assistant message.

findings.title: Scope matches the plan entry, and deferrals go to issues
findings.description:
- The plan's exclusions (`max_file_size_bytes` defaults, #114) are honored.
- Ordering and `--stat` are filed as #137 with the reasoning given (D7), as the plan allowed.
- The neighbouring file-body truncation problem is filed as #138 rather than pulled into this slice.
- The two additions are justified: the `max_total_injection_bytes` skip path (D3) is the same silent failure, only worse, and needs no new branch. The D6 render fix is needed so the synthetic finding doesn't hide a degraded parse.

findings.title: The Part A field set is the minimum, as the plan asked
findings.description: The plan asked design to "pick the minimum that lets a gate decide". D1/D2 put only a three-state `diffTruncated` in frontmatter and send the counts to the header and JSON. The design also explains why the counts are in characters, not bytes, rather than reusing the misleading `*_bytes` names.

findings.title: Interface parity comes from the code structure
findings.description: Every new fact is carried on `ReviewResult` and rendered by the single `format_review_markdown` and `to_dict()`. This meets the plan's requirement that CLI and pipeline behave the same without a second code path. The pipeline `ActionResult.metadata` changes are listed explicitly.

findings.title: Substitution rule fails safe, and its rollout effects are stated
findings.description: D9 is exact and conservative: when in doubt it reports a substitution. Before merge, it is checked against real ids captured from each profile, which answers the plan's OpenRouter question without guessing. The one-time change to metrology identity for OpenAI judges that return dated snapshots is stated openly, not hidden.

findings.title: No NFR applies
findings.description: `900-arch.maintenance-and-refactoring.md` states no latency or throughput targets for the review path, so the slice doesn't need to restate one.
